key_insight: Direct charge injection from metallic nanoparticles to adsorbed CO is strongly material dependent, with hot-electron transfer consistently exceeding hot-hole transfer because the CO LUMO lies closer to the metal Fermi level than the HOMO.
engineering_relevance: The results identify which nanoparticle materials are most promising for photocatalytic designs that maximize direct light-driven electron injection into target adsorbates.
method: Combined ab initio DFT descriptions of adsorbate–metal interactions with macroscopic electrodynamics of localized surface plasmons.
Predicted hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates for large spherical nanoparticles adsorbing CO.
Compared nine metals: Ag, Au, Cu, Al, Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, and Pt.
evidence_signal: Across the nine-metal comparison, Al, Ag, Cu, and Au gave the largest electron injection rates, while Cu and Au showed substantial plasmonic enhancement and non-plasmonic metals showed weak injection.
watch_item: The study is model-based and focused on large spherical nanoparticles with CO adsorbates, so transferability to other sizes, shapes, and surface chemistries may be limited.
paper_title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
